name: Varwof Gateway
description: Varwof gateway operation permissions (management API + data plane)
author: varwof

capabilities.usage: Used to access HTTP/HTTPS backend services (web apps, REST APIs) through the gateway. The most common data-plane capability.
capabilities.when_not: Proprietary TCP/UDP protocol services do not need it; pure administrative operations do not need it.
examples: Access an internal web service through the gateway

capabilities.usage: Used to forward arbitrary TCP protocols (SSH, databases, custom protocols).
capabilities.when_not: Use proxy:http for HTTP services.
examples: Access an SSH service through the gateway

capabilities.usage: Used to forward UDP traffic (DNS, audio/video, games).
capabilities.when_not: TCP/HTTP services do not need it.
examples: Forward a DNS query through the gateway

capabilities.usage: Used to support QUIC/HTTP3 client access.
capabilities.when_not: Legacy TCP clients do not need it.
examples: A web service with HTTP3 support

capabilities.usage: Used to proxy WebSocket long-lived connections (real-time push, chat).
capabilities.when_not: Ordinary HTTP requests do not need it.
examples: Proxy a real-time message push service

capabilities.usage: Used to proxy gRPC bidirectional-stream services.
capabilities.when_not: REST/HTTP services do not need it.

config_key.description: Config keys that may be accessed (empty = all)

capabilities.usage: Used to adjust gateway listeners, routes, and upstream configuration.
capabilities.when_not: Must never be granted for routine data-plane tasks; only needed by operations administrators.

capabilities.usage: Used when configuration changes need to be hot-loaded without interruption.
capabilities.when_not: Tasks with no configuration changes do not need it.

capabilities.usage: Used to dynamically adjust capability-decision plugins (allowlist/denylist/rbac).
capabilities.when_not: Pure data-plane tasks do not need it.

capabilities.usage: Used to manage authorization policy versions and perform rollbacks.
capabilities.when_not: Use ops:plugins for read-only policy viewing.
examples: Roll back to the previous policy version

capabilities.usage: Used to canary-deliver different policy versions per agent group.
capabilities.when_not: Global unified policy is not needed.
examples: Canary a new policy to a specific agent

capabilities.usage: Used to manage the confirmed renewal flow for short-lived certificates.
capabilities.when_not: Scenarios without short-lived certificates do not need it.

capabilities.usage: Used to view online agents and proactively disconnect abnormal ones.
capabilities.when_not: An agent's own tasks do not need to manage other agents.

capabilities.usage: Used to monitor active connections and view access points. Read-only.
capabilities.when_not: No special restrictions; read-only.

capabilities.usage: Used to scrape gateway monitoring metrics (connections/PPS/latency). Read-only.
capabilities.when_not: No special restrictions; read-only.

capabilities.usage: Used to view currently loaded plugins and their scheme definitions. Read-only.
capabilities.when_not: No special restrictions; read-only.

capabilities.usage: Used to view gateway access/connection audit records. Read-only.
capabilities.when_not: No special restrictions; read-only.

capabilities.usage: Used to verify the integrity of the audit hash chain (tamper-evident). Read-only.
capabilities.when_not: No special restrictions; read-only.

capabilities.usage: Used to search audit records by keyword/time range. Read-only.
capabilities.when_not: No special restrictions; read-only.

capabilities.usage: Used to view reference relationships between multi-gateway audit chains. Read-only.
capabilities.when_not: No special restrictions; read-only.

capabilities.usage: Used to probe gateway liveness. A public capability.
capabilities.when_not: No restrictions; typically public.
